title: Traffic is climbing, the HPA wants more pods, and they all stay Pending
intro: A marketing campaign went live at noon. The api Deployment in namespace shop is scaling out as designed: its HPA has asked for 40 replicas. Only 22 are running; the rest have been Pending for ten minutes, and latency is rising. The cluster uses Karpenter to add nodes, and it has always just worked.

steps.prompt: See the Pending pods in namespace shop.
expected_commands: kubectl get pods -n shop | grep Pending
steps.fake_output:
NAME                   READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
api-6c9d7f5b8-2xkq4    0/1     Pending   0          10m
api-6c9d7f5b8-7hm2n    0/1     Pending   0          10m
api-6c9d7f5b8-b4t9w    0/1     Pending   0          10m
... (18 pods)

steps.prompt: Find out why one of them isn't scheduled: describe pod api-6c9d7f5b8-2xkq4 and read its events.
steps.fake_output:
Events:
  Warning  FailedScheduling  10m   default-scheduler  0/14 nodes are available: 14 Insufficient cpu. preemption: 0/14 nodes are available: 14 No preemption victims found for incoming pod.
  Warning  FailedScheduling  9m    karpenter          Failed to schedule pod, all available instance types exceed limits for nodepool: "default"

steps.prompt: Two messages. The scheduler says all 14 nodes are full, which is normal: that's Karpenter's cue. Karpenter says every instance type would 'exceed limits for nodepool default'. Look at that NodePool's limits and current usage.
steps.fake_output:
Spec:
  Limits:
    Cpu:     200
    Memory:  800Gi
Status:
  Resources:
    Cpu:     196
    Memory:  412Gi
    Nodes:   14

steps.prompt: The pool may hold 200 CPUs and already has 196. The smallest allowed node adds 8, so Karpenter can add nothing. The limit was set a year ago as a spending cap. The on-call lead approves doubling it for the campaign. Patch the NodePool default so spec.limits.cpu is 400.
Watch Karpenter act: list the node claims.
steps.fake_output:
NAME            TYPE          CAPACITY    ZONE         NODE                        READY     AGE
default-7xk2m   m7g.2xlarge   on-demand   us-east-1a   ip-10-0-1-21.ec2.internal   True      6d
...
default-q8w3r   c7g.8xlarge   on-demand   us-east-1b   ip-10-0-2-140.ec2.internal  True      48s
default-z5n1d   c7g.8xlarge   on-demand   us-east-1c                               Unknown   12s

steps.prompt: New nodes are joining. Confirm the Deployment reaches its target: check the api Deployment in namespace shop.
steps.fake_output:
NAME   READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   AGE
api    40/40   40           40          200d

resolution: Autoscaling is a chain, and every link has its own ceiling. The HPA did its part: more traffic, more replicas, up to its maximum of 40. The scheduler did its part: no room on 14 nodes, so the pods waited. Karpenter did its part too: it tried to launch nodes and was refused by its own NodePool, whose limit of 200 CPUs had been set a year ago as a cost guard and never revisited as the baseline grew to 196. Nothing was broken. Each component was obeying a limit, and the one that mattered hadn't been looked at in a year. The Pending pod's events told the whole story in two lines, which is why 'describe pod' is the first move for anything Pending; the second line named the NodePool. Raising the limit let Karpenter launch nodes within a minute. Other things that produce the same symptom, and are read the same way: the cloud account's instance or vCPU quota, no remaining IP addresses in the subnets, a pod that asks for a zone or instance type no NodePool allows, or a PersistentVolume pinning the pod to a zone that's full. The lessons are about limits as a system. Know every ceiling between a traffic spike and a served request: HPA maxReplicas, NodePool limits, cloud quotas, subnet sizes, and the database connection limit behind them (systemdesign-incident-004). Alert when usage passes 80% of any of them, so the conversation about raising a spending cap happens in a planning meeting and not during a campaign. And test it: a load test that scales the service to its HPA maximum would have found this limit on a quiet afternoon.
